Messages.Author: Petri Wessman
Messages.Body:
Ok, so let me get this straight: the new NRA limits actions from a
card in play to one per turn. So a vampire with a built-in "attack
minion as (D) action" (Wynn, etc) would be a card in play, and would
only he able to use his/her built-in rush once per turn. Right?

As far as I've understood from conversations on this newsgroup, the
wording of Archon and Templar ("Successful referendum makes the
vampire an X. An X may enter combat with...") gives a rush ability
that is tied to the keyword/title of Templar or Archon, and is therefore
not limited to once per turn. Still correct?

Any other cards and/or loopholes in the game that give this multi-rush
ability?

If not, I don't see this as being too abusive, you still have to both
make the vampire a Templar/Archon and have the capability for multiple
actions per turn. Nice if you can set it up, but votes from a combat
deck should not be too impossible to prevent - if the deck is focused
on passing the votes, it probably won't have too much offensive
capability, leading to the multi-rush being not too scary. I could be
wrong, of course ;)

//Petri
